samples.question: This image shows one round target painted on white paper. The grey page frame and the four short grey ticks near the corners are fixed decoration: they never indicate the answer. A band is one solid area of a single colour inside the target: the filled disc in the very middle is a band, and every complete ring of colour drawn around it is also a band. Neighbouring bands always use two different colours, and those two colours take turns from the middle outwards, so the same two colours reappear again and again no matter how many bands there are. The number of bands, the two colours used, the overall size of the target, the thickness of the individual bands and the position of the target on the page all change from image to image. Count the bands that are actually painted in this image, from the middle disc out to the outer edge of the target, and do not answer from how many rings a target normally has. How many bands does this target have? Answer with exactly one of the integers 3, 4, 5, 6, or 7.
